reason: The text portrays the Israelite people as faithless, complaining, and rebellious. After the spies return, the community murmurs against Moses and Aaron, shows distrust in God despite His demonstrated miracles, and attempts to stone Joshua and Caleb who urge faith. God describes them as a 'wicked congregation' who have tested Him ten times and do not believe in His signs. All adults over 20 (except Caleb and Joshua, who are explicitly distinguished and praised individually) are condemned to die in the wilderness due to their unfaithful response. The ten spies who delivered the negative report die by plague. Only Joshua and Caleb are portrayed favorably, but they are presented as exceptional individuals set apart from the regular people through their distinct faith and divine favor.
